emma (eng-runtime): heads-up — after the kernel/quant rollout earlier today we're seeing a meaningful drop in prefix-cache hit rate for a subset of traffic. noticed at ~10:20 UTC.

raj (sre): ugh. numbers?

marta (perf-eng): from perf dashboards — model=redwood-v2-small, quant=int8-q4_1, kernel=fused-attn-v2. historical pfx hit ~0.88, now ~0.47 for the affected routes.

emma (eng-runtime): perf-bot also alerted: 
perf-bot: "pfx_cache_hit_rate drop (route:/chat/completions) — 88% -> 47% over 30m" :warning:

raj (sre): any errors in logs? eviction storms?

sanjay (infra): quick grep of node logs shows frequent cache-miss traces and a spike in warmup RPCs to key-value service. sample: ```
[2026-03-17T10:22:11Z] pfx_cache: miss key=sha256:3f1a...
[2026-03-17T10:22:11Z] warmup.fetch prefix_id=usr-123 len=64
```

marta (perf-eng): ran a small profile against a replay subset. output: ```
route: /chat/completions
baseline(hit)=0.89
post-rollout(hit)=0.46
most-missed-prefixes owned by high-frequency PLG traffic
```

emma (eng-runtime): hypothesis 1: kernel variant changed internal tokenization/kv-key serialization (ordering or float->int switch) causing different canonical prefix bytes. hypothesis 2: quant profile affects serialization of cached attention keys (unlikely but we saw a serialization marker change in compiled kernels).

sanjay (infra): added: batching heuristics were adjusted earlier (smaller batch boundary for fused-attn-v2). could interact with prefix windowing and produce different cache keys if we include batch metadata in key.

marta (perf-eng): confirmed key schema — we include: model_id + model_version + serialized_prefix_bytes + batch_flag + quant_profile_tag. if any of those change (even ordering) it invalidates cache. I ran a diff on keygen: new kernel build bumped quant tag ordering.

emma (eng-runtime): oh — that explains why only some routes (that hit the optimized path) are impacted.

raj (sre): mitigation options? rollback? quick canonicalization shim?

emma (eng-runtime): short-term plan: 1) deploy a key-normalization middleware that canonicalizes prefix bytes (strip/normalize whitespace, deterministic token->byte mapping) and pins model_version & quant_tag ordering. 2) schedule a rollback of the kernel flag for affected pools if we see user-facing latency regressions.

sanjay (infra): I can push middleware as a feature-flagged hotfix to edge nodes. patch includes: ```
// pseudo
key = sha256(concat("model:", model_id, "|ver:", model_version, "|q:", quant_profile, "|prefix:", normalize(prefix)))
function normalize(s) { return s.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim(); }
```

marta (perf-eng): deploy-bot shows the rollout id for fused-attn-v2 was 2026-03-17-ker-42. we should correlate which nodes took it.

deploy-bot: rollout 2026-03-17-ker-42 applied to pool: prod-gpu-pool-{3,7,9} at 10:05 UTC.

emma (eng-runtime): quick experiment: can we replay a handful of affected requests through the canonicalization shim and confirm hit-rate recovery?

marta (perf-eng): running replay now on prod-copy fixture. will report in ~10m.

perf-bot: replay-job-837 queued -> started (replay subset 12k requests).

marta (perf-eng): preliminary: canonicalization fixes ~85% of the misses in the replay. remaining misses are due to different kv-cache shape (tile ordering) introduced by fused-attn-v2: keys appear to be sharded differently at runtime.

sanjay (infra): that means some misses require compatible kernel-level serialization OR a cache-migration strategy. we could add a key-suffix that represents kernel-compatibility and keep both caches for a transition window. but that's more complex.

raj (sre): what's the risk of leaving the new kernel but with normalization shim? any leftover perf impact?

marta (perf-eng): with shim + canonicalization we recover ~82% of baseline; tail latency unchanged in replays. the remaining ~6-8% gap is warmup-related (different prefetch ordering). Not catastrophic.

emma (eng-runtime): propose: ship normalization shim behind a flag to prod-gpu-pool-3 first, monitor 30m. if hit-rate recovers to >0.8 and no latency regressions, rollout to 7 and 9. simultaneously open a kernel-compatibility ticket to adjust key serialization in fused-attn-v2 build.

raj (sre): +1. i'll prepare a canary alert for error budgets and tail-latency.

sanjay (infra): I'll also add a temporary metric: pfx_key_schema_version so we can observe dual keys and avoid accidental eviction across schemas.

marta (perf-eng): created perf ticket #INF-4821: "prefix-cache schema drift after fused-attn-v2 + int8-q4_1" with reproducer and mini-diff of keygen. assigned to emma + sanjay.

emma (eng-runtime): thanks. i'll create the feature-flag patch and link PR in the ticket. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

raj (sre): if we see any regression after fix, we can rollback rollout 2026-03-17-ker-42 quickly — I have the steps documented.

perf-bot: alert cleared? waiting for canary metrics.

marta (perf-eng): will post follow-up once the canary completes (ETA 40m).
